answer.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (31, 86) converge on simplifying/shortening onboarding producing durable activation gains without noted retention costs. Verifying both before committing checks whether they reflect genuinely separate experiments or overlapping/duplicated evidence, since stacking two similar-sounding memories could overstate confidence. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but that memory explicitly documents a retention cost of 12 points, directly conflicting with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective, so it's deliberately not chosen this week despite the competitive urgency. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are solid but don't address the two internal metrics currently declining. A standard_experiment scale is warranted rather than broad rollout, since even convergent memories deserve a live confirmation before scaling further, and I'm preserving uncertainty about whether the current onboarding/activation dip has the same root cause as the earlier consolidated wins.
